# Motivation

**Example status — sketch:** schemas on this page motivate modeling choices;
they are not evaluated benchmark results.

The central bet behind `relflow` is narrow: when relationships inside a record
carry signal, the model should be able to see those relationships before they
are reduced to handcrafted features.

That is not a claim that every dataset should be nested or every tabular model
should be replaced. It is a response to a class of systems where building the
flat feature row has become a second, rigid modeling architecture.

## The Representation Problem

Important operational data often arrives as related contexts:

```text
customer
|-- profile
|-- transactions[]
|-- statements[]
`-- login_sessions[]
    `-- events[]
```

A conventional pipeline may turn this object into rolling sums, counts, last
seen values, and fixed trailing windows. Those features can be effective. They
also make choices before learning begins:

- which histories deserve a window;
- which order and local relationships to preserve;
- which aggregation periods matter;
- how long each context may be;
- which transformation must be reproduced online;
- which derived features need to change for a new task.

Flattening is therefore not neutral. It is a lossy model of the source record,
implemented in data-pipeline code.

## When Preserving Structure Helps

Use `relflow` when the relationships themselves are plausible signal:

- line-item combinations inside an order;
- behavior within a login session;
- sequences of measurements from one device;
- transactions considered in a separate context from statements;
- nested histories whose useful windows have different lengths.

Use a simpler tabular model when rows are already independent observations or
when aggregates retain everything the decision needs. A flat baseline remains
valuable even for a nested problem: it reveals whether the additional
structure earns its memory, latency, and operational cost.

Preserving hierarchy also does not invent relationships that are absent from
the schema. `Hash` gives repeated identifiers matching representations, but
separate sibling branches pool their tokens before interacting. Cross-context
correspondence may therefore need restructuring or preprocessing so matching
roles meet before pooling.

## Schema As Model Blueprint

RelFlow makes the record schema executable:

- leaf declarations choose datatype-specific validation, tensorization,
  embedding, loss, metrics, and prediction behavior;
- `Branch` declarations define bounded contexts whose children can interact
  before a pooled representation flows upward;
- learning roles choose values to hide and reconstruct;
- `embed=True` chooses representations to expose;
- names and queries bind source values to stable model addresses.

```{python .marimo}
#| echo: true
#| output: true

import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model(
    name="account",
    d_model=64,
    n_layers=2,
    n_heads=4,
    embed=True,
    customer_tier=rf.Category(size=16),
    transactions=rf.Branch(
        length=128,
        overflow="tail",
        merchant_category=rf.Category(size=256),
        amount=rf.Number,
    ),
    is_fraud=rf.Category(mask=True, size=2),
)

model
```

The schema is both a data contract and an architecture blueprint, but it is not
the raw source contract by itself. Optional preprocessors and leaf queries still
decide which point-in-time values enter an observation. See
[Data Flow](core-concepts/data-flow.qmd) for the complete boundary.

## Why Several Local Contexts?

One long sequence forces unrelated items to compete for the same positions and
attention pattern. A tree can give transactions, login sessions, and events
inside each session different lengths and local encoders.

That supports a more faithful hypothesis: event interactions can be learned
inside a session, then the session can be summarized into the customer context.
Transaction interactions can be learned separately before their summary reaches
the same customer.

This is a modeling capability, not proof of better quality. The benefit depends
on ordering, window selection, the availability of sufficient training data,
and whether the target truly depends on local relationships. It should be
measured against simpler baselines on a leakage-safe split.

The [Device Tenure](case-studies/device-tenure.qmd) page is an architectural
case-study sketch, not an evaluated benchmark.

## Typed Fields Share One Training Loop

Numbers, bounded categories, sets, local identities, timestamps, text, and
vectors do not have the same representation or learning objective. RelFlow
uses tensorfields so each type owns those details while every field participates
in the same tree traversal and Lightning loop.

The common interface separates value state from type-specific content. That
lets the model distinguish an explicit null, branch padding, and a value hidden
for reconstruction without assigning those conditions ordinary content values.
See [Built-In Data Types](core-concepts/data-types.qmd) for the shared contract
and each datatype page for its type-specific behavior.

The tensorfield boundary is designed to be extensible. Treat extension APIs
according to their documented support level rather than assuming every internal
base class carries a long-term compatibility guarantee.

## Supervised And Reconstruction Roles

Supervised prediction and masked reconstruction use the same basic question:

> Given the visible context, what should this hidden value be?

`mask=True` always skips a supervised answer and reconstructs it. Other
`rf.Mask` policies can select positions for learned masking, structural
skipping, train-only dropout, or reconstruction. A mask attached to a branch
is resolved once per branch coordinate and applies atomically to all active
descendants. Embedding export does not hide a value or create a loss.

A shared mechanism makes it possible to combine supervised and self-supervised
objectives without creating a separate feature representation. It does not make
those objectives equally useful: masking rates, target weights, and the amount
of signal in neighboring fields remain empirical decisions. See
[Learning Modes & Embeddings](core-concepts/embeddings.qmd).

## Evolving A Schema

Real data contracts and modeling goals change. RelFlow exposes the schema tree
so a workflow can select nodes and update, extend, delete, reset, or temporarily
override them.

Potential uses include:

- adding a supervised target to a pretrained encoder;
- hiding fields that are unavailable or inappropriate for a deployment;
- exporting a branch embedding for retrieval;
- adding a new context after an upstream contract changes;
- comparing an ablated schema with the original.

Shape-changing mutations can require new parameters, and compatible weights do
not guarantee a compatible model meaning. Schema changes need validation,
artifact versioning, and often renewed training. Mutation is a controlled
mechanism for evolution, not automatic transfer learning.

## Inspection Without Causal Claims

Because outputs retain schema addresses, practitioners can inspect decoded
values and embeddings at the root, branch, or leaf where they were produced.
Field-importance workflows can hide selected input fields and measure how a
chosen metric changes.

Those are model diagnostics. They show dependence of this model on this input
under a stated perturbation; they do not establish causality, fairness, or a
complete explanation of a business decision. Governance, authorization,
decision capture, and audit policy remain responsibilities of the surrounding
system.

See [Field Importance](guides/field-importance.qmd) for the diagnostic workflow.

## The Costs Of Keeping Structure

Hierarchy moves representation decisions into the schema; it does not remove
them. Practitioners still need to choose:

- branch lengths and overflow behavior;
- field types and vocabulary capacities;
- model width, depth, heads, and attention modes;
- temporal and identity split rules;
- preprocessing and schema-version contracts;
- the quality, latency, and memory budget for operation.

Long branches increase padding and attention work. Large categorical capacities
increase learned and scored parameters. Deeper trees and additional decoded
targets add compute. Performance claims therefore need workload, hardware,
precision, and batch context rather than a universal observations-per-second
number.

## One Configured Path

Training-serving skew often appears when offline and online systems implement
the same transformation twice. RelFlow keeps queries, optional preprocessing,
tensorization, model execution, prediction writing, and optional
postprocessing on one configured path.

That path only stays consistent when the actual artifact and processor
configuration are preserved. A service that rewrites normalization, loads a
different vocabulary, or changes schema queries has changed the model contract
even if it loads the same weights.

The practical objective is not “no feature engineering.” It is to make the
learned record representation, the data boundary, and their tradeoffs explicit
in one inspectable schema-driven workflow.
